title: Before You Automate a Process, Find Out Why It Exists
excerpt: Processes in small businesses usually are not designed—they grow. Before you remove steps, you need to know what job each one is actually doing.

sections.heading: The hidden function of a step
paragraphs: A step can look repetitive and still be doing important work. An approval might be checking for duplicate charges, surfacing exceptions or giving another team visibility—not simply approving a number.

sections.heading: Map before you automate
paragraphs: Talk to the people who actually do the work. Ask what they check, what they send back, what happens in an exception and what information they need that is not obvious from the workflow itself.
sections.imageAlt: Before and after view of mapping a process before automation

sections.heading: The principle
paragraphs: The goal is not to preserve every step. The goal is to know what you are removing before you remove it. Map the process first. Understand what is really happening. Then decide what to automate.
